narrative: 如果一条走廊、一条铁轨或地毯上的人字形图案指向一个人，那么这个人就拥有了这个目的地，而建筑则拥有了这条路径。如果这些线条越过他们指向远方，那么这个人就成了一道门，而无限的远方拥有了其余的一切。
如果这个地点本身没有真实的方向矢量，这就不是对的工具。在一间平淡无奇的房间里画出暗示性的箭头，是一种图形上的谎言。
一个只需要一张脸的特写，并不需要一条“铁轨”。线条可以是单点透视、两点透视，甚至是一条曲线。
任务是一样的：决定眼睛被迫落在何处，以及那个落点是一张脸、一扇门，还是一片消失的远方。
how: 在布景中寻找真实的边缘：踢脚线、栏杆、一条道路、来自硬光源的一道阴影。摆放摄影机的位置，使这些边缘汇聚于预定的质量块上。
较广的镜头（24mm到35mm）会加强这种汇聚感。长焦镜头则会把线条压平成堆叠的层次，那是压缩效果，而不是指向效果。
除非这条线本身就是荷兰角式的，否则要保持地平线水平。提示词：Leading lines driving the eye to [Subject], rails, corridors, roads, or shadows converging on the figure.
when: 当一个地点本身能够“指向”时使用它：车站、酒店大厅、公路、战壕、教堂中殿。不要在一个实际上只是杂物间的布景里凭空发明汇聚式的家具。
vs: 消失点（Vanishing Point）是平行线看起来相交的地方。引导线可能在画面内永远不会真正相交。
单点透视（One-Point Perspective）是一整套沿轴线构建的结构，带有一个主导性的消失点。引导线则可以只是一段切割凌乱房间的单一栏杆。
对角线构图（Diagonal Composition）即使在没有任何汇聚点的情况下，也能运用偏斜的能量。建筑纹理（Architexture）用材质填满画面，使“指向”变成次要因素。
examples_film: 《闪灵》（The Shining）用地毯、走廊和一辆三轮车的行进路线，指向那些等待着的事物；《猎鹿人》（The Deer Hunter）用钢铁、道路和工业化的边缘，把注意力推送穿越工作空间。
这些线条是地理，而不是贴纸。这是语法，而不是可以照搬的迷宫。
mistakes: 最常见的误用是一张居中的肖像配上随意的建筑背景。破绽是一张位于中间的脸，而墙壁本身并没有指向任何地方。
修正方法：移动摄影机，直到某条边缘真正指向主体，或者放弃这个说法，直接拍一张干净的肖像。

faq.q: 电影中的引导线（Leading Lines）是什么？
faq.a: 它们是画面中真实存在的边缘（铁轨、道路、走廊、阴影、手势），用来把眼睛引导向某个质量块，或穿越整个画面。建筑本身在“指向”。落点是一种选择：一张脸、一扇门，或空旷的远方。

faq.q: 引导线（Leading Lines）与单点透视（One-Point Perspective）有何区别？
faq.a: 单点透视是摄影机正对某个平面、带有单一消失点的构图，通常沿轴线布置。引导线则是任何能够“指向”的矢量。一条凌乱街道上的斜向栏杆同样可以起到引导作用，而不必是库布里克式的走廊。

faq.q: 什么时候该用引导线（Leading Lines）？
faq.a: 当布景本身确实能够诚实地“指向”某处时使用它：一条大厅、一条轨道、一条道路、一座中殿。在一个只需要一张脸的特写中，或在一个根本没有真实边缘指向主体的房间里，就不要使用它。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写引导线（Leading Lines）的提示词？
faq.a: 指明线条和目标。示例：Leading lines driving the eye to [Subject], rails, corridors, roads, or shadows converging on the figure。明确指出材质。如果这些线条应当越过人物继续延伸，也要说明。

narrative: If a corridor, a rail, or a carpet chevron aims at a person, that person owns the destination and the building owns the path. If the lines aim past them, the person is a gate and infinity owns the rest.
It is the wrong tool when the location has no honest vector. Drawing implied arrows in a bland room is a graphic lie.
A close-up that needs only a face does not need a railroad. Lines can be one-point, two-point, or even a curve.
The job is the same: decide where the eye is forced to land, and whether that landing is a face, a door, or a vanishing field.
how: Find real edges in the set: baseboards, rails, a road, a shadow from a hard source. Place the camera so those edges converge on the intended mass.
A wider lens (24mm to 35mm) strengthens convergence. A long lens flattens lines into stacks, which is compression, not pointing.
Keep the horizon level unless the line itself is a dutch. Prompt: Leading lines driving the eye to [Subject], rails, corridors, roads, or shadows converging on the figure.
when: Use it when a location can aim: station, hotel hall, highway, trench, church nave. Do not invent converging furniture in a set that is actually a box of leftovers.
vs: Vanishing Point is where parallel lines appear to meet. Leading lines may never meet in frame.
One-Point Perspective is a full axial construction with one dominant vanishing point. Leading lines can be a single railing cutting a messy room.
Diagonal Composition uses bias energy even when nothing converges. Architexture fills the frame with material until pointing is secondary.
examples_film: The Shining aims carpets, halls, and a tricycle path at whatever waits. The Deer Hunter uses steel, roads, and industrial edges to shove attention through working space.
The lines are geography, not stickers. Grammar, not a maze to clone.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a centered portrait with random architecture. The tell is a face in the middle and walls that do not aim.
The fix is to move the camera until an edge actually hits the subject, or to drop the claim and shoot a clean portrait.

faq.q: What is leading lines in film?
faq.a: They are real edges in the picture (rails, roads, corridors, shadows, gestures) that steer the eye toward a mass or through the frame. The architecture points. The landing is a choice: face, door, or empty distance.

One-point perspective is a camera squared to a plane with a single vanishing point, often on axis. Leading lines are any vectors that aim. A diagonal railing in a messy street can lead without being a Kubrick hall.

faq.q: When should I use leading lines?
faq.a: Use them when the set can honestly point: a hall, a track, a road, a nave. Skip them in a close-up that only needs a face, and skip them in a room with no true edge toward the subject.

faq.q: How do I prompt leading lines for AI image or video?
faq.a: Name the lines and the target. Example: Leading lines driving the eye to [Subject], rails, corridors, roads, or shadows converging on the figure. Specify material. If the lines should continue past the person, say so.
